summary:
Session 2026-11-16 (run late, 15:04 UTC, market open). Portfolio stays 100% cash, no trades. SPY about -1.2% and Nasdaq -1.5% to -2% intraday, so cash is not a drag.

Examined and rejected:
- NVDA/Huang/Megaspeed: new Commerce interim rule needs licences to reexport Blackwell-class chips to SG/MY/TH/ID/BR and limits remote access. DELL/SMCI are already -5.5%. NVDA reports 11-17 after close with ~9% implied move, a binary I can't call.
- BABA: reports 11-19 before open, rents Nvidia chips via Megaspeed, already -48% from its high. About 50/50, no trade.
- HD/LOW: Zelman downgraded both to Underperform. LOW is +27% since the 10-05 low into earnings 11-18, but the pre-market reaction was muted and defensive rotation could hold it up. Conviction about 52%, so no short.
- URGN (CGON Ph3 read-through): the -9% pre-market print had already recovered to -3%. CGON faded from +19% to +11%.
- NX: the -19% pre-market print was stale, the stock actually trades about -0.8%.
- Refiners: crack spread is down to ~$35 but products are still constrained, so no short. Airlines on falling oil: no edge.
- TU, PERI, SMMT, HELP, DRTS: priced, merger arb, or binary biotech.

Context: Anthropic IPO prices 11-18 and trades 11-19 as ANT ($70-78, ~$64B plus a $26B placement, 20% retail). GTA VI releases 11-19. Brent is ~$95 and Hormuz flows are recovering. 10-year yield is 5.13%, a Fed hike is priced for December, and the chip rebound is unwinding.

Next session:
1. Read the NVDA print and guidance after 11-17 close, then look for lagging peers that haven't reacted.
2. Check the HD (11-17) print and whether it resolves the LOW setup before LOW's 11-18 report.
3. Check BABA 11-19 and the ANT pricing and debut.
4. Re-quote any movers-list name before acting, because pre-market prints can be stale.
5. Look for a PUBM-type peer that lags a leader and has a dated catalyst.
feedback: The pre-market movers lists (digest and benzinga) show prints that are stale or thin: NX -19% actually traded at -0.8%, and URGN -9% was -3% by 15:05. A flag in the digest for pre-market prints under about 1% of average volume would help. The scan tool's pre-market column does show the latest one-minute price, which was useful. The session also ran after the open, so the "pre-open" framing in my notes didn't apply. Benzinga and invezz read_page fetches fail most of the time, so I fall back on search-result content. A free-text news search tool, not only per-ticker, would help find second-order links.
